name: Model_Instance_BuildNodeBoundsChecked
signature: u32 Model_Instance_BuildNodeBoundsChecked(u32 model, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c, u32 d, u32 e)
summary: Validating wrapper around Model_Instance_BuildNodeBounds: first checks that the model handle is usable (0x0057B308) and only then builds the node bounds, returning 1 when both steps succeeded.
evidence: NEW: the callee is now the confident Model_Instance_BuildNodeBounds (0x00566030 alias, same body as the readable function), so the wrapper is not a generic 'setup' but the checked entry to the node-bounds builder; the old name hid which operation was being set up.

name: maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList
signature: void maybe_Model_BuildAimPartList(u32 owner, u32 partA, u32 partB, u32 partC)
summary: Reached from Model_AttachAimParts; only the prologue survived decompilation: four arguments are copied into locals and a two-element array of 0x40-byte descriptors is constructed in a 428-byte stack buffer. The 1384 bytes after that call were lost, so the aim-part contents stay unknown.
evidence: No new named neighbour beyond Model_AttachAimParts (the caller). The only surviving call is std_ConstructArray(buf, 0x00535B54, 0x40, 2); that is a construction detail, not evidence for what the descriptors hold, so confidence stays below 0.5.

name: Fs_Worker_ProcessQueue
summary: Body of the filesystem worker thread: pops open requests from the queue at +0x1BCC, releases each request's node list, updates the per-type byte counters at worker+type*0x28, recycles the request into the ring buffer at +0x2000, and when the open queue is empty waits on the +0x35C queue before running the open path (0x0056F7A4) for the next request.
evidence: NEW: both queue helpers are now named - Os_QueueTryPop on +0x1BCC/+0x35C and Container_RingBuffer_Push on +0x2000 - and the open path callee is the now-named Fs_NamedObject_Open, which is exactly the 'pop request, process, re-queue' loop the name claims. The unaff_r7 in the pseudocode is a decompiler artifact for the popped pointer (its damaged spot is the only one in the body), not a missing argument.

name: Fs_NamedObject_Open
summary: Opens one named object from an archive: marks the request 'opening' (state 2), looks the name up, attaches the stream on success or records an error, then sets state 3 and pushes the request back to the archive's completion ring buffer at +0x790.
evidence: NEW: every callee in the body is now named by a confident function - Fs_NamedObject_ReadRecord, Fs_Stream_SetBufferLimits, Fs_NamedObject_FindAndRead, Fs_NamedObject_AttachStream and Container_RingBuffer_Push - and its only caller is the named Fs_Worker_ProcessQueue. The whole open sequence is therefore confirmed rather than guessed.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenTexture
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_DrawScreenTexture(u32 gfx, void* cmd, void* tex)
summary: Emits the GPU command sequence that binds an overlay texture for one draw: binds the texture handle, builds the texture/colour state chain (0x0065660C..0x00656BCC), a six-slot command node and finally writes the texture descriptor, advancing the command cursor stored at cmd+4.
evidence: NEW: the command helpers on both ends are named - Gfx_CmdList_BindTexture at the start and Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureDescriptor / Gfx_CommandNode_BuildChain4 at the end - and both callers are overlay draw paths (Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen and its B variant). That supports 'overlay draw command', though whether the texture is the screen copy specifically is still open, hence 0.5.

name: Script_CallWithStackTop
summary: Pushes null, copies the VM's top-of-stack value into a managed reference and calls the supplied callback with it, then releases the reference - the plumbing used by the script event/book parameter setters when they must hand the current stack top to a callback.
evidence: NEW: the VM callees are now named (Sq_VmReadStackSlot at index -1, Sq_VmPop, plus the ref init/clear helpers), so the 'read top of stack, pass to callback' reading is confirmed; the callers maybe_Script_SetEventParams / maybe_Script_SetBookCommandParams are also consistent with passing script arguments along.

name: Gfx_ModelPart_BuildDrawParams
summary: Builds the draw parameters of one model part: copies the part matrix into the node record, packs the part's scale fields into the colour/scale block, stores the two per-part values at +0x7C4/+0x7C8 and sets the 'visible' flag bit 0.
evidence: NEW: the node-side callee is the named Camera_BuildFrustum (called for part 0) and the caller is the named Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses, so this is part of the overlay draw submission rather than arbitrary matrix code. The offsets (+0x754 part record, 0x7C stride) now match the named bone-matrix builder.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildPartMatrices
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildPartMatrices(GfxModelInstance* self, int part_index, u32 arg3, int cmd)
summary: Rebuilds the packed bone matrices of the three draw slots of one model part (0x8C8 for the base part, 0xB2C for the others) through Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildBoneMatrices, then re-submits the base part's draw data and clears the two cursor fields.
evidence: NEW: the called builder is the now-named Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildBoneMatrices, and the only callers are Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses / the overlay begin-draw path, which is exactly where per-part matrices are rebuilt before submission.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_SetNodePosFromArgs
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_SetNodePosFromArgs(SceneActor* self, u32* scene, u32 actorIndex, int nodeIndex, u32 valueSource)
summary: Writes a fixed-point position into one node (0x2C stride) of the scene record at *scene + actor*0x278: two float reads are packed as (low | high<<16) into node+0x14 and the third into node+0x18, selecting between layout +0x14 and +0x28 by the actor's mode byte (+0x28 is 9 or 0x0B) and whether the source callback was invoked.
evidence: The caller is now the named Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildBoneMatrices, but the two value readers (0x00508AF8 / 0x005080D0) remain unnamed, so it is still unclear whether the values come from an animation track, a path or the caller's arguments - the 'FromArgs' part of the old name is the weak point. Name kept, summary now spells out the two different field layouts.

name: Gfx_SpritePool_AllocFromResource
signature: u32 Gfx_SpritePool_AllocFromResource(GfxSpritePool* pool, GfxResEntry* res, u32 capacity, u32 arg4)
summary: Allocates a free index from the pool bitmask, composes the 0x02000000|index handle, and instantiates the sprite from the resource (Gfx_Sprite_BuildBuffers when the resource is loaded, otherwise Gfx_Sprite_BindResource); returns the handle or 0.
evidence: NEW: both instantiation branches are now confident names - Gfx_Sprite_BuildBuffers and Gfx_Sprite_BindResource - and the sibling pool constructor stores 0x9C-byte sprite entries, so the pool is the sprite pool, not a generic 'scene node pool'; the old name pointed at the wrong object family. The only damaged spot is the unaff_r7 register, which is simply the bitmask pointer reloaded from pool[0xd] - the surrounding loop and both instantiation callees are intact, so the name is safe.

name: Gfx_SpritePool_Construct
signature: void Gfx_SpritePool_Construct(GfxSpritePool* self, GfxAllocator* alloc, u32 nodeCount, u32 spriteCount)
summary: Builds the storage of a sprite/popup pool: a free-list-linked array of spriteCount 0x9C-byte entries (each with six 0x14-byte sub-objects), a bitmask, and nodeCount 200-byte node records (each with six vec3 at +0x38); previous storage is freed through the allocator vtable first.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the named Battle_PopupPool_InitEntry and the allocation unit matches the sprite entries used by Gfx_SpritePool_AllocFromResource, so 'sprite pool' is supported. Confidence stays at 0.5 because the same layout also backs battle popups, i.e. the exact owner class is not settled.

name: Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass1
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass1(SceneRenderer* self, void* dst, void* node_list, u32 arg4, u32 flags)
summary: Builds the opaque pass of the draw list: collects the visible nodes with Gfx_Scene_RenderPass1, creates one draw entry per node through Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject (pass 1) and links the result into the caller's list; on allocation failure the collected node list is destroyed and 0 is returned.
evidence: NEW: both ends of the body are now confident names - Gfx_Scene_RenderPass1 at the top and Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject / Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeListByIndex in the failure path - and the pass-2 sibling below uses the same shape with mode 2, which is exactly the two-pass split.

name: Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass2
signature: u32 Gfx_Scene_BuildDrawListPass2(SceneRenderer* self, void* dst, void* node_list, u32 arg4, u32 flags)
summary: Builds the transparent/effect pass of the draw list: collects nodes with Gfx_Scene_RenderPass2, creates draw entries through Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject with mode 2 and links them; failure releases the collected list through Gfx_Scene_DestroyNodeListB.
evidence: NEW: byte-for-byte the pass-1 function apart from the now-named Gfx_Scene_RenderPass2 and mode 2 in Gfx_Scene_AllocEntryForObject, so the pass-1/pass-2 pair is established rather than guessed.

name: Gfx_Scene_ReleaseSubBuffer
summary: Frees a scene sub-buffer (owner + element pointer pair) through the owner's allocator vtable slot +0x14 and zeroes all four words, so the owning scene can be torn down without keeping stale pointers.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now the confident Gfx_Scene_Release and Gfx_Scene_ReleaseEntryPools, both operating on the four-word block at scene+0x94 - the release path the name describes.

name: Ui_ModelView_SetCharacterText
summary: Fills a model-view window for a newly selected character: copies the global render/camera words, resets the four text containers at +0x160/+0x188/+0x1B0/+0x1D8, releases the old motion path and composes the name plus up to three description blocks through Ui_ModelView_ComposeCharacterText.
evidence: NEW: the composition callee is now the confident Ui_ModelView_ComposeCharacterText (called four times with textBlock[0] and textBlock[1]->f_80/f_90/f_A0) and the other caller is maybe_Ui_ModelView_SetSelectedCharacterB, which secures the 'set the character shown in this view' reading. Confidence 0.5 because the old body also carries the temp-allocator prologue, which is noise.

name: maybe_std_InitStaticArray
summary: One-line thunk: constructs an 8-element array of 4-byte elements from type descriptor 0x005906C0 in a 768-byte stack buffer. Ghidra marks the call as non-returning, so the code after it (and therefore any purpose) is unrecoverable; this looks like a compiler-generated static initialiser.
evidence: The only callee is still std_ConstructArray and the caller is a UI skill-panel routine; the array type 0x005906C0 remains unnamed, so nothing distinguishes it from any other guarded static array. Name kept as a generic initialiser.

name: Field_LampGimmick_ApplyParams
summary: Applies a lamp/gimmick parameter block to the current glow object: converts the block's Euler angles from degrees to radians, spawns the glow when it is missing, writes colour/cone/attenuation values into the glow record (+0x7C..+0xC4) and caches the processed threshold in params[1].
evidence: NEW: both neighbours are now confident names - Field_LampGimmick_FindGlow and Field_LampGimmick_SpawnGlow - and the object it writes is the one those two return. The old 'Gfx_Scene_ApplyLightParams' attributed the write to the render scene instead, which the body does not support; it is a field lamp gimmick parameter applier.

name: Math_EulerToRotation
summary: Converts three Euler angles into the three basis vectors of a rotation: reduces each angle modulo 2*pi, builds a half-angle sin/cos quaternion with the software trig helpers and multiplies the three quaternions, writing the result to out[0..2].
evidence: NEW: the callers are ActorWarp and ActorWarpToMapJumpLocatorID, which both pass an actor's rotation field (iVar6->f_c) and consume three floats - a rotation conversion, not a matrix/scene routine. The axis tables at 0x007E7018/0x007E7024/0x007E7030 confirm the per-axis quaternion construction.

name: Field2D_Sprite_BeginChipWalk
signature: void Field2D_Sprite_BeginChipWalk(u32* out, u32 map, u32* cell)
summary: Starts a chip walk from the current cell: fills the four-word walker state with the cell (or with the cell one row below when the cell itself is not walkable) and points its +0x10 list head at itself; when neither cell is walkable the state is cleared and the list head is null.
evidence: NEW: the walkability test is the confident Field2D_MapChip_IsKind(map, cell, 1), so the routine is a map-chip walk starter as named. Its other 'caller' (Field2D_Sprite_ComputeGlyphUVs) only shares the module, so 0.5 rather than higher.

name: Gfx_ReleaseNodeHandle
summary: Destroys a scene/effect node through a wrapper handle: installs the wrapper vtable at out, unlinks the node from its owner's child list, detaches it (Field_DetachSlotObject), runs the node's virtual release slot +0x40 with reason 4 and releases its effect nodes.
evidence: NEW: the teardown callees are now confident names (Field_DetachSlotObject, maybe_Gfx_ReleaseEffectNodes) and the callers run it on the member at object+0x70 during scene teardown, matching 'release node handle'. The wrapper object written to out is a smart-pointer style holder, which the summary now states.

name: Font_GlyphQuad_Ctor
signature: GlyphQuad* Font_GlyphQuad_Ctor(GlyphQuad* storage, u32 arg2, u32 palette, u32 animator, u32 arg5)
summary: Constructor of the second glyph-quad class: installs its vtable, runs Font_GlyphQuad_CreateFromDescriptor, clears the derived fields, creates the sprite actor/animator, stamps the animator mode byte at +0x129 and attaches the base attachment built by maybe_Font_GlyphQuad_InitBaseAttachment.
evidence: NEW: the base constructor callee is now the confident Font_GlyphQuad_CreateFromDescriptor and the attachment step the named maybe_Font_GlyphQuad_InitBaseAttachment, so this really is the derived glyph-quad constructor rather than a render helper.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePathMotion
summary: Advances a gimmick along its path: steps the phase (+0x1C by +0x18), clamps it against the curve table at +0xC indexed by +0x14, sets the 'finished' byte +0x20 at the end, then writes the sampled position and tangent into the caller's frame record using Field_Path_GetPosition / Field_Path_GetTangent.
evidence: NEW: both path readers are now confident names, so the routine is path motion sampling, not a 'curve timer' - the timer is only the phase input. The body is still decompiler-damaged around the binary search and it silently uses an undeclared second argument (the frame record), so confidence stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateSelectionCursor(FieldGimmick* self, int* arg2, int* arg3)
summary: Per-frame cursor upkeep: clears the gimmick handle when no UI window is open (UI core +0xD84 < 1), and when the stored reference at +0x14 has gone stale calls the context's virtual +0x14 and clears +0x20; either way it then ticks the target marker at +0x1D7C.
evidence: NEW: the marker update is the named maybe_Battle_TextWindow_UpdateTargetMarker and the handle helpers now carry names (Field_Gimmick_TickHandleRef), but the class that owns +0x1D7C is still unclear (battle text window vs field gimmick), so the name keeps maybe_ and 0.45.

name: maybe_Game_DataManager_NotifyA
summary: Two-instruction notification thunk: reads an argument passed in r3, calls Game_GetDataManager and forwards the manager pointer to func_0063F7BC. Identical body at 0x005E88F0 (variant B).
evidence: NEW: the only named callee is Game_GetDataManager, so the old 'Field_Object_NotifyGlobal' subsystem was wrong - nothing here touches a field object. What func_0063F7BC does is still unnamed and the argument comes from an unaff register, so the name stays a low-confidence placeholder.

name: maybe_Game_DataManager_NotifyB
summary: Same body as 0x005E88D4 - Game_GetDataManager followed by func_0063F7BC(*manager) - a template copy of the same notification thunk at a second address.
evidence: NEW: the named callee Game_GetDataManager shows the old 'Field_Object_NotifyGlobalD' label pointed at the wrong subsystem; the forward target and the register argument are still unknown, so this remains a low-confidence placeholder.

name: maybe_Save_CopyChecksumTable
summary: Copies a static 512-byte table from 0x0072E93C into a stack buffer and then into the caller's buffer with the aligned copy helper; called once from Save_Crypto_Context_Init, which stores it in the save context's auxiliary-table slot.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Save_Crypto_Context_Init, which fixes the context (save crypto) but not the meaning of the 256 u16 entries - the checksum/Blowfish-polynomial reading is still unproven, so the name keeps maybe_ and the summary now says 'static 512-byte table' rather than asserting a checksum alphabet.

name: Save_Config_ApplyParamToTree
summary: Recursively applies one parameter value to a configuration tree: for the node it calls virtual slot +0x10 four times (indices 0..3) with the value and then recurses into every child of the list at node[5].
evidence: NEW: both callers are confident names - Save_Config_ApplyRootParam (0.80) and Save_Config_ApplyNodeParam - and they pass a parameter value and the save-config tree root; the old 'Save_CryptoKey_ApplyToTree' assumed a Blowfish key schedule, which the four-slot virtual dispatch does not support.

name: Fs_Resource_Reset
summary: Full reset of a resource slot: runs the release virtual slot +0x28, frees the packed handle entry when it is still registered, re-tags the handle word, then runs virtual slot +0x1C and clears the state byte - i.e. the recycle path used instead of the partial release at 0x005F9138.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Field_LevelData_Reset and the handle free is the named Pack_FreeHandleEntry, which is exactly a 'reset this resource slot for reuse' sequence. Confidence 0.5 because the virtual slots themselves are still unnamed.

name: Sq_Vm_AllocInstanceBlock
summary: Allocates a variable-size Squirrel instance block: (members-1)*8 + 0x34 + extra bytes, initialises it with the VM/format info through maybe_Script_SqValueList_Ctor and points the +0x20 tail pointer at the requested extra space.
evidence: NEW: the initialiser is now the named maybe_Script_SqValueList_Ctor and the field layout (+0x14 format, +0x24 member count, +0x58 tail size) matches an instance/class block. Confidence 0.5 because the VM fields are still only named by offset.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleaseActiveSceneObjects
summary: UI teardown thunk: fetches the UI core through Ui_GetCore and calls Ui_SceneObject_Release on it, i.e. releases the currently active UI scene objects.
evidence: NEW: both callees are confident names (Ui_GetCore, Ui_SceneObject_Release), which shows the old 'Script_UiSystem_Suspend' was the wrong subsystem and overstated what happens: there is no suspend/resume state, just a release call. The caller is unknown, so 0.4.

name: BattleScene_ApplyMonsterScale
summary: Copies the current monster's display size into the battle scene's shared layout object: looks the monster id (scene+0x5D0) up in the DataManager and stores 2*height and 2*(width+depth) plus the fixed 0x42200000/0x43A00000 constants at layout+0x1018..+0x1024.
evidence: NEW: the callers/siblings are now named BattleScene_ApplySceneModels and BattleScene_SyncUnitModels, and the lookup target is a monster record (func_0063DF60), so the 'monster scale into the scene layout' reading holds. Confidence 0.5 because the three written constants are only partly understood.

name: BattleScene_DispatchUnitVariant
summary: Dispatches unit-variant setup from the battle work byte +0x4201: value 6 calls BattleScene_BuildKeyframes, 7 calls the variant-2 entry and anything else calls BattleScene_BuildUnitKeyframes_2.
evidence: NEW: all three branch targets are now confident names of the BattleScene unit-keyframe family (the caller list also corrected the earlier 'Menu_OpenItemEntryWindow' mislabel), so this is confirmed as the variant dispatcher. Confidence 0.55 because the byte +0x4201 itself is still only 'the scene variant'.

name: Field_Level_InitSpriteSets
summary: Initialises the field-level work record: clears its flags/handle words to the 0xFFFFF000 'none' sentinel, then creates the sprite sub-set and sprite set containers and three further embedded blocks, returning the base pointer of the constructed record.
evidence: NEW: the two container creators are now the confident Gfx_SceneSpriteSubSet_Create and Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_Create, and the embedded blocks the named maybe_Field_LevelWork_InitBlockA/B, which supports the name; 0.5 because the routine also clears many non-sprite fields.

name: Field_SceneObject_ReleaseInstance
summary: Releases a spawned field scene object: installs the base vtable, clears the sprite parts / frees the attached handle when +8 is set and runs the virtual +4 of the object at +4. Used on the failure paths of the Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable variants and by Ui3D_InitEffectPairFromRecord.
evidence: NEW: Gfx_SpriteParts_Clear is now a confident callee and the callers are the named spawn functions, so this is the 'undo a spawned instance' path. Confidence 0.5 because the class it finally belongs to (scene object vs effect pair) is still open.

name: Ui_TextEntry_Reset
summary: Resets one fixed-size (0x108-byte) text entry: clears the formatted buffer at entry+8 with the sprintf helper and points the active string at entry+4 back to the inline storage at entry+0xC.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now the named Ui_ShopItemInfo_FillStats and maybe_Ui_ProfileWindow_RefreshStats, both of which refill exactly these 0x108-byte entries, which supports 'text entry reset'. Confidence 0.5 because the entry array owner (0x007AC834) is unnamed.

name: maybe_ItemBag_CountValidSlots
summary: Counts the bag slots 0..0x59 (90, the DQXI bag size) that are non-empty (0x0066B534 returns 0) and whose type byte from 0x0066AF08 is not 0xFF.
evidence: The loop bound 90 matches the known bag size from FACTS.md, but both accessors (0x0066B534, 0x0066AF08) are still unnamed and the owner object is not identified, so 'valid slots' cannot be tightened to 'occupied slots' or 'usable slots'. Name kept.

name: maybe_ItemBag_CountItemsOfType
summary: Counts the bag slots 0..0x59 whose type byte (0x0066AF08) equals 9 - i.e. one specific item kind, not an arbitrary type argument.
evidence: The 90-slot bound points at the item bag, but the only callee is still unnamed and the constant 9 has no known meaning (kind/category/equip flag), so the name stays generic and below 0.5; the summary now names the constant so a reader can follow it.

name: maybe_Monster_SumRecordedCounts
summary: Walks all 0x413 (1043) monster ids, and for each id whose record has a non-zero field +0x22 adds the per-id counter at owner+0x3AE4+id*4; the total is clamped to 0x1869F (99,999) and returned.
evidence: NEW: the loop bound 0x413 and the data-manager lookup func_0063DCA4 line up with the monster table, and the identical table walk in 0x0062A4BC proves the +0x3AE4 array is per-monster, so the old 'Battle_Unit_CalcActionRange' (a float range calculation) was wrong: no action id, no distance, no float. What the counter means is still open, hence 0.4.

name: maybe_Monster_CountDistinctRecordedKinds
summary: Builds a 65-word bitmask over the record field +0x22 of every monster id present in owner+0x3AE4 (also setting the bits of the three related ids found through the table at 0x007273A4), popcounts it and returns that number clamped to 999.
evidence: NEW: the same per-monster table and func_0063DCA4 lookup as 0x00629FEC, plus a popcount over the collected bits: this counts distinct kinds/values, it does not build an encounter mask for later use. The old name suggested a returned/stored mask while the function actually returns the count (the header signature 'void' is a Ghidra slip). What +0x22 denotes is still unknown.

name: Container_ValidateHandle
signature: u32 Container_ValidateHandle(u32* table, u32 index, int checkVirtual)
summary: Validates a tagged handle: for index < 0x83 it reads table[index*2+0x250], requires the 0xB-bit generation tag to match the global handle table at 0x007B80C0... (indexed by the low bits) and, when requested, the object's virtual +0x34 predicate; on failure it returns the 'stale' sentinel with the caller's tag patched in.
evidence: NEW: it is called by four confident handle users - Event_GetOrAddActorSlot, Field_FindObjectByMode, Field_GadgetList_FindOrAddByHandle and Ui_ResolveObjectHandle - all of which need the 'is this handle still valid' answer, so the name is confirmed. The exact tag arithmetic is decompiler-muddy, hence 0.55.

name: maybe_Model_IsInstanceRegistered
summary: Lazily creates the shared model object, resolves the object referenced at obj[2]+0x6C with Field_FindObjectByMode(...,3) and returns 1 only when the returned handle's generation tag matches the global handle table.
evidence: NEW: the lookup callee is the confident Field_FindObjectByMode and the test is the same tag comparison as Container_ValidateHandle, so this asks 'is the instance still registered', not 'has a renderable model'. The singleton it builds is unnamed, so 0.4.

name: Field_Scene_RectIntersectsSetA
signature: bool Field_Scene_RectIntersectsSetA(SceneWork* work, int* rect, int layer, int type)
summary: Rectangle hit test against the scene's rect set at +0x590 (count +0x594): for every entry whose type (+8) and layer (+0xA) match and whose owner passes func_0062F0B4, it tests whether the rects overlap; returns 1 on the first overlap.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Field_Scene_IsPointVisibleByModeB and both members of the pair take a 4-int rectangle and do a rect-vs-rect overlap test - the old 'IsPointInsideRectSet' claimed a point test the body does not perform.

name: Field_Scene_RectIntersectsSetB
signature: bool Field_Scene_RectIntersectsSetB(SceneWork* work, int* rect, int layer, int type)
summary: Same rectangle hit test as 0x0062E38C but over the second rect set at +0x5F0 (count +0x5F4, type bytes +0x608); the 3D-fallback branch of Field_Scene_IsPointVisibleByModeB.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Field_Scene_IsPointVisibleByModeB and the body is a rect-vs-rect overlap test identical to set A, so the 'point inside' wording of the old name was wrong.

name: maybe_Actor_FindByField28
summary: Linear search over the field object manager's pointer array: returns the first live entry (id byte at manager+0xC+id set) whose record field +0x28 equals the requested value, or null.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now the confident ActorWarpToMapJumpLocatorID and Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotPlacement, which suggests a locator/anchor id, but the companion at 0x0062F514 matches +0x19 instead and no named field exists for either offset - so the name stays offset-based and below 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_Slot_IsLast
summary: Resolves the object named by the owner's +0xB0 handle (Menu_Cursor_Resolve) and returns 1 when its slot index +0x270 equals the current slot count - 1.
evidence: NEW: the resolver is now the confident Menu_Cursor_Resolve and the comparison target is the count field under UI context +0x130, which fits 'last slot'. The caller is the low-confidence maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_HandleInput, so which panel this closes on the last slot is still open; 0.45.

name: Ui_Slot_GetState
summary: Getter: returns the state byte at +0x2C9 of the object resolved from the owner's handle, or 0xFF when no object is present. The value is a returned byte, not a discarded void result.
evidence: NEW: the resolver callee is the confident Menu_Cursor_Resolve and the callers (Ui_JockeyPanel_Close, maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_OnDecide) store the byte in their per-slot record before firing events, i.e. they consume a value - so this is the slot state getter, not a check.

name: maybe_Ui_Slot_GetScale
summary: Getter for a float at +0x2A4 of the resolved slot object with -1.0f as the 'no slot' default; the decompiled body only shows the call because the return travels in s0. Callers compare it with a per-panel constant and store it into the work grid at +0x2A264.
evidence: The resolver is now the confident Menu_Cursor_Resolve, but the field's meaning (scale? progress? threshold?) rests on the caller comparisons that are themselves unnamed, and the decompilation is damaged (the float return was dropped), so the name keeps maybe_ at 0.45.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_GetSlotScaleY
summary: Returns the +8 field of the UI layout record selected by the overlay mode byte (+0x281), defaulting to 7.0f when the mode is 0, multiplied by the global float at 0x007A724C; the counterpart at 0x00634D74 does the same with +4 and 1.75f.
evidence: NEW: the DataManager lookup is now recognisable (Game_GetDataManager + func_0063D6B8 with the mode byte) and the constants 7.0f/1.75f are readable, but the field is still only 'the second layout metric' and the float return is lost in the decompilation, so 0.4.

name: maybe_Battle_CanEquipOrUse
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_CanEquipOrUse(BattleActor* self, Actor* actor, int actionId)
